original_question: Let X be a separable Banach space that fails to have type 2 - epsilon, or fails to have co-type 2 + epsilon, for some epsilon > 0. Must X contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 8, where the paper isolates a type/cotype special case of Godefroy's broader Problem 7 on non-isomorphic subspaces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's official target almost verbatim: X is assumed separable; the hypothesis is exactly that X fails to have type 2−ε or fails to have co-type 2+ε for some ε>0; and the conclusion asked for is the existence of continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces. This is precisely the wording of Problem 8 in Section 6. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, specify that 'subspaces' means closed linear subspaces of X and that 'non-isomorphic' means non-isomorphic as Banach spaces (i.e. no bounded linear isomorphism between them).
If you want the cardinality spelled out explicitly, replace 'continuum many' by 'a family of cardinality 2^ℵ0'.

The paper presents this as a special instance of the broader Godefroy problem for separable non-Hilbertian spaces, motivated by the Basis Problem; that surrounding scope should be mentioned in the justification, but not added as an extra hypothesis. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

No extra assumptions such as reflexivity, existence of a Schauder basis, unconditionality, or weak-Hilbert structure belong in the question itself; the weak-Hilbert case is mentioned only as a known positive instance. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
refined_question: Let X be a separable Banach space which, for some ε>0, fails to have type 2−ε or fails to have co-type 2+ε, in the usual Banach-space sense. Must X contain a family of 2^ℵ0 closed linear subspaces that are pairwise non-isomorphic as Banach spaces? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 8 exactly, not the broader neighboring Problem 7. In Section 6 the authors first state Godefroy's Problem 7 for separable non-Hilbertian Banach spaces, then explicitly 'isolate an instance' of that problem connected with the Basis Problem, namely the type/cotype formulation in Problem 8. They also note one known positive case: separable weak Hilbert spaces not isomorphic to ℓ2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))
